newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end broadly down on overseas jitters.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end broadly down on overseas jitters.

text.p: Malaysian shares closed broadly lower amid speculation of Middle East hostilities, as well as fears of a possible drop on Wall Street and higher U.S. interest rates, dealers said.

The benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks closed down 10.19 points to 1,204.39, and the Second Board index of small-capitalised stocks was down 14.92 to 547.85. The broad EMAS index shed 2.50 to 340.25.
"All the markets are following each other right now. The markets are not very stable because there's no support, as many fund managers are on holiday," said Vickers Ballas' Irene Tan.
Stock markets around the region ended around one percent lower.

"The S&P Futures went limit down, the speculation that there had been a bombing in Iraq and a lack of local leads have all made the local market extremely jittery," said an analyst at a foreign brokerage house in Kuala Lumpur.

Sime Darby was up 15 cents to 9.70 ringgit after the company said it had received approval from Malaysia's central bank to start negotiations with Oriental Bank Bhd to acquire a majority stake in the bank.
